newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish festival says Monroe porn film authentic.
newsitem.headline: Spanish festival says Monroe porn film authentic.

text.p: Organisers of a Spanish film festival claimed on Thursday a 1947 porn film purported to feature Marilyn Monroe was authentic and they planned to show it, despite claims it was a fake.

The grainy, six-minute black-and-white film showing a bare-breasted blonde engaging in explicit sex acts has provoked a flurry of interest among collectors and a storm of protest from the Hollywood legend's estate.

Mikel Barsa of promoters Barsa Promociones said the film's authenticity had been verified by experts. He said he was convinced it was a rare, if sordid, image of the 21-year-old Monroe when she was still the little known Norma Jean Baker.
"Several American experts in physiognomy (face recognition) have certified it as authentic," Barsa told Reuters. "It's her."

But the American Film Institute, which festival organisers contended had authenticated the film, on Thursday reiterated it had had no official contact about the short movie and was not in the business of authenticating such films.
However, AFI Director of Communications Seth Oster told Reuters an AFI employee had written an unauthorised letter on the institute's headed notepaper about the film.
"An assistant librarian without the knowledge or authorisation of the AFI, used AFI stationery to express a personal opinion." The employee has been fired, he said.
Also, magazine publisher Hugh Hefner, whose Playboy published nude photos of Monroe in its first issue, said he had seen the porn film and concluded it was "an obvious hoax."
"To the professional eye, these images taken from the film do not remotely resemble the real Marilyn Monroe from the period (1947) when the movie was supposedly made.
"This is one of a number of similar posthumous hoaxes involving Marilyn Monroe. It is the price of fame," he said in a statement.
In the film, the Monroe, if it is indeed her, looks chubbier and lacks the plastic surgery that helped make her into a 1950s sex symbol.
But according to agents and lawyers of Monroe's estate -- she died in 1962 -- the film is more likely a hoax and an attempt to degrade the actress posthumously.
"It is really quite sad that someone would do this to someone who was loved so much," Anna Strasberg, licensing agent for Monroe's estate, said when contacted in New York.
She denied any knowledge of the film and, when asked if it could be a hoax, said: "I know it is."
Irving Seideman, attorney for the Monroe estate said he too knew nothing about such a film, adding: "The estate will be conducting a vigorous investigation of the falsehoods."

Barsa Promociones spokesman Mario Prades said his firm had doubts about the veracity of the film when first contacted by the anonymous collector who had purchased it for a few dollars at a Paris flea market in 1977.

But Barsa had thoroughly tested the contents of the 16mm episode and had certificates, proving its authenticity. But he said they could not publish them because to do so would compromise the collector's identity.

"We had a certificate from a Spanish expert, but we still didn't trust it and sent it to the United States and they confirmed that it was authentic and sent us a certificate," Prades told Reuters Television in an interview.
The reel of film was tucked in among six others that had probably been part of a private library built up during a time when pornography was not shown commercially, the festival organisers said.

Whether a true testimony of the harsh road to stardom, as Barsa believes, or a sick publicity stunt, the organisers of Spain's First Record and Film Collectors Festival in the northeastern town of Vila-seca are not complaining.
"Everyone is interested in this film. The publicity has been tremendous," spokesman Angel Vaque told Reuters. "We were planning to have four showings on Feb. 1 and 2, now we may add two more days."
